notes: The one table that says which picture the game draws for what. Nothing in the code names a file in Art/: to swap a picture, replace the sheet (a <Name>_sheet.png plus its <Name>_atlas.json) and, if its name changed, change the one line below that names it. Every sheet is scaled on load so its typical sprite is `size` node spacings across, where one node spacing is the length of a typical road on the map, so a replacement drawn at any resolution needs no other change. Art/README.md walks through a swap.

backing.notes: What the map draws behind some icons as they load, so the PNGs stay as drawn and the players' cards show them as they are (Q61). An icon under `circled` sits on a disc of `fill` with a contour in the colour given, `contour` thick as a share of the disc's width, its picture centred and scaled so the smallest circle round it spans `picture` of the disc's width, or its own share under `pictures` (above 1 the picture reaches over the contour: the swords, Q230); `size` above is then the disc's width. An icon under `filled` has a disc of `fill` under its picture, as wide as the picture and hidden under its rim, so the gaps in it show that colour. Any other icon is drawn as it is.

site_dot.notes: The dot in the middle of every site's node until the site is claimed (Q80): `size` across as a share of the node's width, in the brown of the roads.

island.notes: [Q170] The map is an island floating in the sky. `underside` is the rock hanging under its two front edges: a picture under Art/, and the three points in its pixels where the map's left, bottom and right corners go. The picture is stretched between those points, so a replacement drawn at any size only needs its own three. The left and right points sit a little in from the rock's ends, so the rock reaches right up to the map's side corners, where it is cut off flush with the map's back edges (681). It is drawn over the ground, and the stone tops that rise above the line through those points fade out over `fade` of the picture's pixels, so they blend into the ground's edge (670, 679); as they fade they are blurred, up to `blur` of the picture's pixels at the top, and stay sharp on the edge itself (832, 833). `greens` turns its moss and ivy towards the map's forest green: each green's hue turns `hue` degrees, its saturation is multiplied by `saturation`, and it is darkened by `darken` (0 as bright, 1 black); the stone, roots and palest sunlit spots stay as drawn (830, 831). `sky` is the picture behind the map. It fills the map's box, stays put as the map is dragged and grows a little as the map is zoomed in (676-678; SKY_ZOOM_GROWTH in apps/web/src/page/sky.ts). `color` is its average colour, shown in its place while the picture loads (680). `shade` darkens both, from 0 (as drawn) to 1 (black): `light` on a light screen, `dark` on a dark one.

sounds.notes: The sound effects (Q63), each a list of files under Art/ and a volume (1 plays a file as it is). A sound with several files uses them in turn, so a walk's footsteps are not all alike. All but `purchase` are placeholders made by Art/tools/make_sounds.py from the samples Andrei picked by ear; `purchase` is the cash register Andrei supplied (Q190, 777); a replacement drops in over the file, or goes in under a new name changed here, and loses its placeholder flag. WAV or MP3 plays in every browser.

shadows.notes: Some supplied sheets bake their drop shadow in as an opaque flat grey, which would sit on the terrain as a grey patch. The loader turns the colours listed here into a translucent dark shadow instead, at `opacity`. No sheet in use needs it: the sheets packed from Art/originals/ by Art/tools/pack_sheets.py have their shadows made dark and see-through as they are packed, at the same strength.

adjustments.notes: Edits made to a sheet as it loads, so its PNG stays exactly as supplied. `brightness` lifts the darks and midtones (each colour channel c, from 0 to 1, becomes c^(1/brightness), so white stays white; 1 leaves it). `saturation` scales how far each colour sits from its own grey (1 leaves it, 2 doubles it). `outline` draws a contour round every picture on the sheet, behind the picture and over its shadow, `width` thick as a share of the sheet's typical sprite so it grows and shrinks with it. A sheet with no line is drawn as supplied; no sheet in use has one, since the art is drawn as its artist made it (Q59).
